summary: Russell recounts the later efforts to find Johnson and the Frenchman who reached him.

blocks.x: Very old. He was 90 then. That was about two years ago, 1960 or so. Maybe 1959 that I talked to this fellow from France. I have some notes on it, I couldn't find him today. But I'll also find those notes and add them to this Bill Johnson interview. I will take a practice trying to find him. I would have gone, I would have gambled some of our Tulane money as I said, which is expensive. I would have paid $50 for an interview. If I would both offer him $25 or $50 expenses gone out there, I would have done that. I would have gone at that time. But I don't believe it would be worth it now to try to find him. And there's a good chance he's dead at this time. That was two years or more ago. I doubt that we could find him. But if there's any way that you would ever find him, it would be still good to meet him. I don't think we'd get enough information to make it worthwhile.

But in 1940 or 41, on the way back from California about that time, I stopped and saw him for the last time. He was in the same apartment on South Parkway and had these pictures, which I'd hoped to get.
